correctness.rationale: Primewise verification of RESULT.md:55–101: when q does not divide n, Lucas gives consecutive unit coefficients at j=1 for units digit at least two, or j=q^a when n−1=q^a u and u>1. Both are interior witnesses. When n=q^a u and u>1, choose a supported base-q digit of u so subtracting the corresponding power leaves the digit at position a nonzero. Then the first binomial is a unit, the next has valuation a by the adjacent-binomial ratio, and division by n cancels it. For n=q^a, the identity using the row q^a−1 gives valuation a−v_q(j)−v_q(j+1) in the adjacent product divided by n; this is at least one and exactly one when an interior j has valuation a−1 (j=1 for prime n). For n=q^b+1 only the four Lucas positions 0,1,q^b,q^b+1 can be units. The two boundary pairs have valuation b−v_q(2); the strictly intermediate pairs have valuation at least two. In the claimed exponent-two cases, at j=q^(b−1), the two Pascal sums each have terms of valuations 1 and b, hence achieve exactly two jointly. The exceptional n=3,5 and odd q with b=1 give valuation 0, 1 and 1 respectively from the boundary entry. The supports from n and n−1 are coprime. A separate exact Pascal-row recursion checked all 598 rows n=3..600, including divisibility of each product by n.
residual_risks: Finite corroboration only; the unbounded result rests on the primewise proof.

value.rationale: Interior peak counts are a standard Catalan refinement; excluding the two unit endpoints makes their common divisor a natural arithmetic invariant. The theorem characterizes the precise contribution of the predecessor, including odd-prime squares and binary boundary effects at composite indices, and replaces finite tables or individual divisibility conditions with a test on two integers. Its significance is that exact structural classification, not a new general result on prime powers.
residual_risks: No valuation distributions or gcds over different peak ranges claimed.
